title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review initial benchmark results on Redwood hosted vs dedicated configs, confirm access and IAM for VPC onboarding, discuss KV cache tuning and batch sizing, and align next steps for security docs and overnight large-scale run. Customer reported token throughput variability; SE to follow up with revised runbook and perf config.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share SOC2 and security whitepaper and KMS integration notes - due 2027-01-05
Priya Nair: Upload micro-benchmark scripts and suggested config (batch size, quantization) to shared drive - due 2026-12-31
Tom Rivera: Confirm VPC peering details and provide Bastion host access for Redwood engineers - due 2026-12-30
Carlos Mendes: Validate dataset access and confirm PII masking approach, reply in thread - due 2027-01-04
next_steps: Jordan to send pricing/commit options for Dedicated and hosted fallbacks
Run 8-hour overnight load test with updated batch settings (Priya & Tom to coordinate)
Security team to schedule 30-min follow-up on SSO/KMS integration week of Jan 4
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-29 10:30 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (NexaHealth CTO), Aisha Khan (NexaHealth ML Eng), Tom Rivera (NexaHealth DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda — 1) access and env readiness, 2) benchmark recap, 3) tuning recs, 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Carlos: Yep, that's good. we wanted to focus on the variability we saw in the tokens per second during the long run this past tuesday.
[00:32] Priya: Right, so we pulled the logs and there are a couple of things. one is the batch sizing was set to auto which hit emi — um, edge cases with our prefix cache. the other is the KV cache warmup wasn't happening because the requests had slightly different prompt prefixes.
[00:50] Aisha: Just to clarify, by prefix cache you mean the KV cache for the attention state? sometimes the transcript uses KV and I've seen it as K-V cache or key value cache.
[01:05] Priya: yes, KV cache. sorry for the slur, sometimes auto-transcripts call it keevy. the main impact was we saw 15-20% higher latency on tail percentiles when the cache missed.
[01:25] Tom: we can control that on our side by normalizing prefixes in the preprocessor. i can add a normalization step.
[01:30] Carlos: and how does that translate to cost? is it the batch size or the cache misses that drive up cost?
[01:40] Jordan: both. if you reduce batch size you get lower latency but higher per-token GPU time; cache misses cause repeated KV recompute which kills throughput. our rec is to use a modest batch (8-16) with prefix normalization and enable persistent KV between bursts.
[01:58] Aisha: do we need Dedicated for that, or can Hosted handle persistent KV?
[02:05] Priya: Hosted supports prefix caching, but Dedicated gives you more control over eviction and length of cache, plus predictable throughput. for the POC we've been running hosted to move quickly.
[02:20] Carlos: ok, timeline wise, if we opt for Dedicated later, what's the rollout? we have compliance constraints, SOC2, and we need KMS integration.
[02:32] Jordan: we can do a Dedicated trial — typically a short reserved pool for the POC. KMS/HSM integrations are supported; i'll send the integration notes. also SOC2 doc attached in the deck link — see notes.
[02:50] Tom: about the VPC peering — we tried the peering and got a firewall issue, so the Redwood IPs were blocked at our egress. i opened a ticket but need to coordinate the exact CIDR list.
[03:05] Jordan: i'll send the egress cidr list. Priya, can your team do a quick checklist for ports and IPs?
[03:12] Priya: yes i'll drop a checklist in the shared folder. also adding micro-bench scripts so they can run in their env.
[03:22] Carlos: great. quick question on logs and audit — do you stream audit logs to our S3 or do we pull? we prefer push to our acct.
[03:32] Jordan: we can push audit logs to a customer S3 with cross-account role; that's in the security doc. i'll include the role sample.
[03:40] Aisha: returning to perf — we ran two configs: hosted default and hosted with recommended tuning. the tuned run improved median latency by ~18% but tail was still spiky. the logs show occasional GC-ish pauses on the service.
[04:00] Priya: GC pauses? you mean system-level pauses on their side or on the runtime?
[04:06] Aisha: the host-level. we will capture traces but my guess is noisy neighbor on the cloud instance we used for the long run.
[04:15] Jordan: noisy neighbor is a classic for shared hosted runs at scale. that's where Dedicated helps with predictable tail latencies.
[04:25] Tom: ok, so immediate next step is both: we normalize prefixes and rerun the overnight load on hosted with tightened batch sizes, and Priya sends scripts.
[04:34] Carlos: agree. how about the data retention note — we have PHI concerns. how does Redwood handle retention and redaction?
[04:42] Jordan: by default logs are retained 30 days for POC but we can configure retention per account; plus you can enable automatic PII redaction in the pipeline or push logs to your managed S3 to control storage. i'll include the redaction options.
[05:00] Aisha: also, can we enable SSO with our Okta? we need SAML/SCIM for user provisioning.
[05:08] Jordan: yes, we support SAML + SCIM, i will loop in security to do quick config.
[05:16] Priya: one note on quantization — we tried 4-bit for the model and saw minimal quality regression on our eval set but 12% faster token throughput. if you have strict quality metrics we can run AB tests on a holdout prompt set.
[05:34] Carlos: that's promising. we have a suite of prompts in the benchmark spreadsheet, i'll give access.
[05:41] Jordan: perfect, please share the sheet link in the thread.
[05:45] Tom: about the overnight run — what metrics should we collect? we want RPS, p50/p95/p99 lat, token/sec, cache hit rate, and memory usage.
[05:58] Priya: yes those plus GC traces and kernel-level GPU utilization. we'll add a Prometheus scrape for the metrics and a Grafana dashboard reference.
[06:10] Aisha: if we find quality regressions after quant, what's the rollback path?
[06:16] Priya: we can pin model version and fallback to full float variant. Redwood's smart routing can fall back to another variant if quality thresholds are breached. it's a canary-like rollout.
[06:30] Carlos: ok good.
[06:35] Jordan: quick recap and owners — Jordan to share security docs and cidr list; Priya to upload bench scripts and suggested configs; Tom to confirm peering and provide bastion access; Carlos to validate datasets and share prompt suite. any other items?
[06:55] Tom: i will also check our quotas for egress and get back.
[07:00] Jordan: cool. do we want a follow-up security-only 30-min next week?
[07:06] Carlos: yes week of Jan 4 works.
[07:09] Aisha: works for me too.
[07:12] Jordan: perfect. i'll send calendar invite.

[45:00] Jordan: jumping ahead — Priya, you mentioned a config tweak that reduced tail latency. can you share exact flags?
[45:08] Priya: sure, it's primarily setting batch_size to 12, disable aggressive prefetch, enable persistent_kv=true and increase kv_eviction_threshold from 0.2 to 0.6. also set affinity to dedicated-cpu for the io threads. i'll write it up.
[45:30] Aisha: do you have an example run command?
[45:34] Priya: yes, i'll paste it in the shared script. it's in the repo: /shared/poc/bench/run.sh (link in thread).
[46:00] Jordan: any blockers for the overnight run?
[46:05] Tom: need the checklist from Priya and the egress cidrs. after that we can schedule the run tonight.
[46:12] Jordan: i'll send both within the hour.
[46:15] Carlos: perfect. thanks everyone.

[54:30] Jordan: final quick notes — i'll attach SOC2, KMS notes, and sample S3 role in the following email. PRIYA will upload the bench artifacts. Tom will confirm peering. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time. thanks all.

End of transcript. Attachments/links mentioned: security_whitepaper.pdf (link), bench_scripts.zip (link), benchmark_spreadsheet.csv (link), runbook.md (link).
